preamble: Fortition of a rhotic to the voiced alveolar stop [d] closes an approximant or tap into a full stop at the same place of articulation. In Oti-Volta (Gur), Eddyshaw reconstructs a Proto-Oti-Volta *r, probably the approximant [ɹ], that became d in Core Eastern Oti-Volta (Mbelime, Nateni, Ditammari, Byali) both word-initially and as the initial of the EGG-gender singular suffix *-rɪ́, while Western Oti-Volta has y, Gurma and Yom have l and Nawdm keeps r.

examples.note: Forms in Eddyshaw's transcription: POV *r = the approximant [ɹ], y = [j], j = [ɟ], ɩ ʋ = [ɪ ʊ], a tilde below a vowel marks nasalization; POV = Proto-Oti-Volta. Compare Moba lúób̀, Mooré yòobé.
The suffix *-rɪ́ shows the same d; Waama keeps r (nɔɔre).
Mbelime yédē 'two' has y instead of d.
